notice: Training template. Adapt to your quality system.

templates.title: Incoming inspection checklist
templates.use: Record what was checked on the dock, what was sampled, which lot the sample came from, and what the disposition is — so a quarantine can be explained a year later.

templates.title: MSL exposure log
templates.use: Track the clock on every moisture-sensitive reel: floor life, what has been counted against it, what is left, and what the bake decision is.

templates.title: Stencil inspection sheet
templates.standard: IPC-7525 (area and aspect ratio), IPC-7526 (stencil cleaning)
templates.use: Compute the release indicators for every aperture on the board and decide which need a stepped foil, before the first print.

templates.title: Reflow profile log
templates.use: Record the thermocouple readings, compute the ramp rates and the time above liquidus, and decide whether the profile is inside the window.

templates.title: Design feedback pack
templates.standard: The plant's own production data; the placement acceptance and the fiducial geometry are Board X's
templates.use: Turn a production result into a design ask with a number in it and a price on it, so the design team can act on the next revision.

templates.title: Test coverage model
templates.standard: The plant's own defect model and screen probabilities; node coverage is a test-program measure, not a standard's
templates.use: Work out what a series of screens actually catches, class by class, instead of quoting the share of joints that carry a probe.

templates.title: Cleanliness and coating record
templates.standard: IPC-TM-650 2.3.25 (ROSE); the customer's limit is a customer value, not the reference one
templates.use: Report an ionic result with the area it was divided by, the blank it was subtracted from and the local site it hides, then work out the coating volume from the film the drawing asks for.

templates.title: Rework and repair record
templates.standard: IPC-7711/7721 (rework and repair method), with the width limit from IPC-A-600 (20 % Class 2, 10 % Class 3)
templates.use: Record what the repair did to the board — heat, contacts, the trace it touched — and judge the damage against the class the customer requires.

templates.title: Selective solder program record
templates.standard: IPC-A-610 (joint acceptance), IPC-7711/7721 (rework of what the program gets wrong)
templates.use: Check the nozzle against the joint it has to fill, and put the cycle time on the sheet before anyone promises a rate.

templates.title: Wave solder run log
templates.standard: IPC-A-610 (joint acceptance); the wave windows are the machine's, taken from the course and the equipment datasheet
templates.use: Record the settings a wave run actually ran at, compute the contact time and the pot margin each one gives, and keep the findings on the same page as the record that explains them.

templates.title: Through-hole fill record
templates.standard: IPC-A-610 (vertical barrel fill, and the inner-layer exception)
templates.use: Record the barrel fill on every through-hole joint, compute it against the board thickness, and disposition it against the class that applies — without letting the thermal-plane exception become the rule.

templates.title: Placement audit record
templates.standard: IPC-A-610 (placement and soldering criteria); machine capability targets are the plant's, not a standard's
templates.use: Turn two fiducial readings into the translation and the rotation the placement report leaves out, and carry each one out to the parts that sit furthest from the rotation centre.

templates.title: SPI print record
templates.use: Record every deposit's volume against the nominal the stencil actually cuts, and keep the mean from hiding a print that has two humps.

templates.title: 8D problem report
templates.use: Take a defect from containment to closure in the standard eight disciplines, with the numbers that prove each one.

templates.title: Defect Pareto sheet
templates.standard: Pareto analysis; defect classification per IPC-A-610 class
templates.use: Rank defect types by count, carry the cumulative share, and show which few types account for most of the loss.
